answer: Only 80% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. Because the basalt ledger attributes every share, the atlas audit shows the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, and as a result it pays the kernel fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 27 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
